chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdillah al-Hasani, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Sulayman slave of Tirbal, from Hisham al-Jawaliqy, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
— what is meant by it? He said: 'His Transcendence.'

key_terms.تَنْزِيهُهُ: His Transcendence (tanzih) — God's absolute freedom from all imperfection and likeness to creation
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ: Glory be to / Glorification — the formula of divine praise, cited here from Quran 23:91

ai.seo_question: What does 'Subhan Allah' (سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ) mean according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines the Quranic expression 'سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ' (Glory be to Allah, Quran 23:91) as 'tanzih' — God's absolute transcendence, meaning He is utterly free from every imperfection, deficiency, and resemblance to creation. This concise answer reflects a cornerstone of Shia theology: that glorification formulas are not merely liturgical but carry precise doctrinal meaning affirming divine incomparability.
